_comment: What the SOCOM II NTSC r0001 disc (SCUS-97275) produces on its way to a buildable ELF, so that
tools_py/disc_to_elf.py can tell a stranger whether their run came out right instead of hoping.
Every value here is a FACT ABOUT the disc -- a size, a sha256 digest, a guest address, a build
id string -- and none of it is the disc's content: nothing here can be turned back into a byte
of the game. The same choice was already made for launcher::kSocom2R0001ElfSha256, the digest
the launcher and the runner's preflight pin (ps2xShared/include/launcher/launcher_config.h);
inputs.SCUS_972.75.sha256 below is that same digest and must stay equal to it.
A null value is one nobody has measured yet: the first run records it and says so, and the
recorded value is committed with a note saying which disc it came from. A value that is here
and disagrees with a run is a refusal, never a quiet overwrite -- see check_value().
disc.* is the image's shape and a difference there is only a note (R231): a re-built or
differently padded image of the same disc holds the same bytes at other LBNs, and the three
files this chain reads are pinned by digest under inputs.
dnas.variants are the four (key table, cipher core) address pairs inside DNAS.BIN that
dnas_selfdecrypt.py's research path derives from a Ghidra decompilation. They are recorded here
so the chain runs without a Ghidra project; they are only meaningful for the DNAS.BIN whose
digest inputs records, which is checked first.
